Content: We know our neighbors and our neighbors' neighbors!
Neighbors look out for each other and help raise each other.
We check in on everyone regularly, and everyone knows their responsibility to check in on others.
We also build deep relationships across differences, instead of flocking together with those “like us”
You see people from all kinds of places, traditions, and cultures everywhere you look.

Our individual priorities take a backseat to our individual needs. Individually we recognize we are better together rather than divided by our ideologies to be heard and seen as individuals but a greater calling to oneness. We see and feel one another and the richest of ways.
The future is small and therefore sacred - small communities of people tending to each other's collective needs and well being. Small is intimate. Small is healing.
A staple in the community is a huge fruit tree - a place to get fruit, but also to congregate, tell stories, share knowledge. Central gathering place.
We walk more these days, and though fear is part of our everyday, we find solace in each other as communities again. The slogans from the past: we keep us safe, take on new meaning.
Children and adults each have more than 10 people to turn to when they feel alone, lost or sad, or about to do something that may hurt another person.
We live in family units, communities, elders and children equally cherished and cared for.
Play is at the heart of community ... a constant rhythmic dance ...welcoming all ways of being.

All people help the person in front or behind. We bring everyone with us. We welcome everyone with open arms. We teach people how to be in the flow of what is needed. The whole circle is protected. No one is better than anyone else.

All people help the person in front or behind. We bring everyone with us. We welcome everyone with open arms. We teach people how to be in the flow of what is needed. The whole circle is protected. No one is better than anyone else.
The local community feels vibrant and restorative. It feels like a vacation right in our own homes and backyard, reducing the desire to travel to far off places just for vacation.

Everybody gets along; landback for everything to come back together; feast together; no more fighting over money; starting gardens; community; dismantling schools; drug dealers stay in jail so they don't get out and do it again; pimps, fentanyl, and all things killing Mother Earth are gone; sunshine, trees, birds, flowers, kids playing happy; EVERYbody gets along
There is space for people to be heard. Real community spaces. Where real community members are heard. They go on as long as they need to go on for the needs to be met.
We know how to welcome and we understand that this place is not for everyone and we care for those that have chosen to be somewhere else.
There is a sense of community and belonging. Everyone is housed in equally sized housing in circles with a community/public center.
We have gotten good at welcoming new people to communities. There is mentorship.
Teaching skills of that area. Helping with the connection to the place, rhythms, and methods.
We live in interconnected webs of small communities, connected through relationship.
We gauge how well we're doing as a community through joy.

It is important that we physically build together what is needed- homes, communal spaces. Community spaces support communal sharing. If a neighbor needs to mow their lawn, the neighbor with a lawn mower lends it. Doors are opened. Kids are raised in community. Every day responsibilities are shared and rotated.
There are no fences in the neighborhoods. Neighborhoods eat together. Laughter can be heard throughout the day-and grief, challenges, and successes are shared and celebrated.
Our spiritedness led to big shifts in community habits.

Speaking of space, there is space! There is quiet. There are laughs and laughter that rings through neighborhoods as part of the ever present conversation, storytelling, and sorting things out. We eat together. Life is vibrant. Deep greens. Bright blue. Yellow and oranges.

There are hubs where different things flourish - science, art, growing foods, building community, health and wellness. And tended relationships across the hubs so that everyone can access what they need. Every morning, people can join play in their blocks, alleyways, farms to connect and laugh and ground in the relationships of neighbors before folks head to their hubs.
Ecosystems and culture touch.

Villages form to share resources and teach each other, learn from others how to care for, listen to, understand our neighbors. Family has evolved from single units formed through blood and marriage to include sisters and brothers from our others. These new families unite around ways of respectful listening, talking, learning, and being that push our communities towards sharing and caring for us all. Diversity thrives - biodiversity, diversity of thought, diversity of people.

Our differences bring each other together to learn new ways of being, to taste new flavors, to hear new sounds, and embrace new sights. Difficult conversations are not null, but occur and people support each other in having the difficult talks. Religion exists but is recognized for its power to calm the mind and soul and create social connections. No one religion reigns supreme.

There is a tenderness and connection among communities who share a place, an understanding of interconnectedness and the time to cultivate relationships, with relatives - not just familial and human but all of the creatures and living beings in a place.

Villages do not ask you to prove your right to be there. In fact, you are welcomed with water so clean and so clear that your energy is buoyed upon the first swallow. You are welcomed by all ages (littles, bigs, elders)... whoever is closest to the village "entrance" is the one who does the welcoming. Some times people hover around the "entrance" because they LOVE doing the welcoming. And the welcomes are in all forms: Poetry, song, dance, hand holding and guiding but always welcomed.
Our hearts and minds are open as we consider each other’s needs and our own, and create and recreate solutions that ensure we can all participate.
Community, all are provided for, everyone has a role.
Collective community is created and sustained through stories, practices and experiences.

Communing will be an everyday thing. There will be a nightly commune. Neighborhoods will have fires and food at night. Look at the sky. The trees. The lake. They will talk about issues of the day. They will share grief, etc.
We will teach and learn about the stars by night – looking at the night sky in community.

No one with a voice believes they can’t sing. People know the music that is inside of them. Community is organized around dancing and other things that feed soul – rather than things that feed addiction.
When we need something, the first place we go is to our neighbors.
Crisis will be a call to commune rather than to isolate. Everyone has space, knowledge, and wholeness to sit with others and help when needed.

Spaces are safe enough to be vulnerable. People share artwork. Thoughts. Questions. Voice, etc. We leave pieces of artwork to be shared in other’s homes. We operate like a community wide art library. It is a deep and purposeful practice of community building, but the new generations think its normal.
Communities are made out of smallish clusters, and gather in various formations on a daily/nightly basis.
Communities are organized around what people need and don’t need–and the consultation of nature. We know we are simply another part of the earth.
Our wealth will be in our ability to care for one another. People living into their purpose. Leadership of so many forms.
The lifestyle is slower. We do our best to be good neighbors every day.

We hold each other in community through crisis. It involves giving space, unwavering respect, respecting autonomy by giving options, rehumanizing, and following our intuition for the wellbeing of all.
Struggles are embraced in community–not pushed out to the periphery. We share in the responsibility.

People live in communities of care. The cultural norm is caring for one other. The priority is always on caring for people who are having a harder time. Spirit and healing pathways are oriented to this, and to the wellbeing of everyone so there are always people to care.
No nation states. Communities that are highly mobile and built around natural rhythms. A global consciousness fueled by shifts in technology.

Energetic pulsing: conscious and creative interaction. Consciousness that is held in terms of shared purpose. Awareness of unlearning, re-learning and knowing with multiple intelligences beginning with the land and children. We walk in the consciousness of the differently abled. We are able to transmit knowledge in different ways to each other.
When harm interrupts the balance, we restore it with love and accountability.
Ho’oponopono is practiced regularly. The community's conflicts are not allowed to turn into scars.
We put in the time and energy for restorative justice - creating shared norms of mutual respect - towards greater harmony.
We are fully in community, so balance has been restored. People no longer need so much stuff as individuals, but rather care more for community.
Society is built around a core desire to embrace the other.

Living more in community hubs and sharing. Not to become enclosed circles, but always welcoming other people in, welcoming visitors, experiencing each others’ communities. Be inviting and allow others in to learn from one another. Learn love and embracing within our community, and this allows us to then be able to connect with other communities.
Communities live by the principle that institutions and structures are designed and governed for the benefit of all.
Community is focused on beauty, freedom, truth, wisdom… Purpose, creativity, and a connection to nature guide who we are and what we do.
Everyone contributes, no one harms the others. What you need is available. How do these things exist and not harm each other? How do we make things free and available?

People exist in wholeness and in connection, web of need and strength of walking together. We raise people who care, engaged in solving and mutuality. We have deep practices for honoring and for tending to collective thriving.

-In every community the people create The Center, a place where everyone goes to be vulnerable about their fears and encourage a sense of hope. It is a place where conflicts among individuals and groups gather to story-tell their way back to a grounded place centered on compassion, hope, and embraced humanity. The Center is a place to feel safe, in one’s full dignity and a reinforced sense of belonging. To come back to intactness. It is a place to feel unsupported. A place where harm is acknowledged and tended to. We cook meals and eat together. We sing, dance and create art together. We care for each other’s wounds. We sit in silence and listen to each other’s heartbreaks and hearts exploding from joy. The Center is a place where we deeply connect to our own humanity through each other’s, thus preventing wars in the heart and home, the homeland and the homes and hearts of others.
We gather in community circle with consistent rhythm.
Two Spirited people are viewed as wise people in community due to perspectives…duality, etc.

Potential for how each person will contribute to the new advancement of human well being will be assessed thru play, observation and community circles of elders who are honored for the generations of experience. The communities will live in small tribal groups, that provide opportunities for deep connection, understanding and knowledge of their tribes. There will be intentional practices of honor and celebration of the differences and individual gifts and talents in each tribe.
People live in interconnected and diverse communities of proximity and choice.

We will have become so good at bridging differences. People who do not see the world in the same way will gather together. It will be normal to enjoy being in community with people who see the world differently.

Communal, community care, eating together, sipping tea, new ways to deal with conflict and difference….Binaries not real…reciprocity. Love is love and we are accepting- we are all losing these false ideas of who we are.

Community where art, dance, storytelling are main things. What would we do if we were not being productive for money? Stewarding art, growing, harvesting, caring, tending, preparing food, appreciating the Earth.
I draw the community I grew up in. A prosperouse, safe cooperative. Physical and economic security. Children go out to play safely
Original of Translation: Dibujo. La comunidad en la que crecí. Una cooperativa próspera, segura. Seguridad física y económica. Los niños salen a jugar sin peligros.

Content: We accept and respect difference
People are able to share their wisdom and gifts in communes, in connection with nature.

Communities have a soul practice that is embodied. When they eat food they immediately know all of the beings that contributed – the bird that pooped the seed, the earth, the sunshine, the salmon, the sea.
Every member of the community feels like they are connected to multiple Spirit Hubs with clever, punny names – Mighty Chondria, Big Love, etc. based on their core practices.

Date/Circle Name: 1/11/25 BIPOC outdoors - Maji ya Chai Two Harbors MN
Content: Communities are organized differently - densely and less dense populations…all living off the land.
Individual small communities that they care for on their own. Dependent on values. Children and leaders centered. All of life is oriented on that.

Local communities and where needs are met for all. Sharing skills, teaching in intentional ways to pass on knowledge. Responding collectively to the needs of communities. Less primacy of the immediate family in terms of housing and more ways of sharing. Different approaches of configurations of how people form families and are housed.
Multigenerational wisdom + knowledge exchange communities
community is responsible to and for one another
Community accountability.
Knowledge and sharing skills as a community

The criminal justice system is now bifurcated into the “inayan” and “solidago” systems; the former named for the Kankanaey concept that it is a community value to prohibit an act that causes harm to another; the latter from the idea to make whole. Any offense is treated as an opportunity to make all parties whole, rather than punish.
Communities have collective fire hearths, inside and out, where people of all ages, especially older and younger, gather weekly to share stories of future and past time.

The activities of the community are centered around care. Caregiving to meet people’s needs is most important. Other duties and roles are addressed once care is covered. Parents are compensated for their roles in tending to the nurturance and development of the next generation

And we're just so committed to ensure that there would be many different expressions for people to package their spirit and to express them as much as we can.  And people brought to the party all of their skills and talents and things that they had preserved over the years.  Milk fists and dried berries they had collected.  Things they had woven.  Pictures they had drawn.  
And they shared them together.  And people were invited to take what they needed and what they desired and leave what they had to share.  And all the people were of all different walks of life, different colors of skin, and they all had equal access to the gifts that everyone had brought.  And if somebody couldn't reach up to the table, then someone else would hold them, ask them what they wanted, and help them access that.

Family units, blocks where people belong. People are brought into the world with a sense of purpose related to contributing their talents to the community. There is communal eating and sharing, where people contribute what they grow. There is mutuality, sharing, love.
All private property has been converted to communal usage. We feel good about being free. We let it go.
Everybody has a future (in the community).  The question is how does the community responds when people do their worst.  We understand everyone still has a future.

Unity only working because we are in a circle.
No hard edges, circles everywhere, community. 
Ovals in motion and vibrant. Circles, cycles, belonging.
The ocean is taken care of by everyone in the community.

Communities are smaller, there are no borders, strangers are welcome, everyone has the resources they need to survive. Everyone works to support the collective – choosing work that aligns with their skills and what lights them up.

Communities are filled with music, art and the smell of food.  No one goes hungry because there is enough for everyone to eat at the community center–a beautiful place where communities gather daily for meals.
Communication among community is telepathic

Knowing we are all connected is no longer a concept, we deeply feel this. It is no longer a concept, when one person hurts we all hurt. We literally feel this. Because of this vicarial experience, the way we resolve conflict, share our feelings, our home, the land we live on, communicate and care has been transformed towards deep collective care, universal experience and thriving lives.

We are sitting together in community because we know someone is grieving.  There is so much space for that grief.  Some people in community specialize in holding the grief.  There are those that bring the laughter.  There are those that bring the tissues.  Cries are welcomed.  Laughter is welcomed.  We know that all can be held within the circle.  People who are grieving are asked what is going to be most helpful to them, and the community fills in the gap.  The community has developed rituals and practices to tend to the grief.  We no longer expect people to get over grief in a linear way.  We honor, morn, and celebrate loss.

We talk about the period where modernizing things meant dehumanizing ourselves and buying into scarcity.  Now we come together to celebrate what we generate together – we have gratitude – we know there is enough.  Village life has returned in all corners.  We cultivate our own contributions (gardens etc.) so that we can share the abundance.  People line up in neighborhoods and houses when certain things are ready to be harvested.

A number of times a year, the local police and fire departments host community building events, and every member of the staff introduces themselves - almost no one is nameless, everyone is familiar with everyone else. They are welcoming to those they don’t recognize, too. Even with this camaraderie, there isn’t a forced feeling of having to stop every time you see someone you know. We enjoy our independent lives, too, but when we need any sort of assistance, we can rely on someone in our neighborhood to be able to point us in the right direction.
We look out for each other.  We no longer surveil each other
Communities would have stronger intergenerational relationships outside of blood relatives. Young people learning from our elders, gaining the wisdom necessary after the great collapse.
Community is not seen as a one for one system. There aren’t IOU’s for sharing a cup of sugar. There is a reliance on each other, without feeling like a burden.
We will be able to be with each other in deep community across distance to help each other solve problems, to mourn when we lose each other, to celebrate births.
People are constantly having conversations with each other / in conversation / in order to remain connected and build together.  There are community assemblies at the micro level and the macro level
There are community cookouts every weekend. Community dinner every night.
There are frequent circles, folks present something different to each other every time they connect.
People have a sense for real community and belonging. All of us are well cared for at every age and stage of life.
We have a deep sense of accountability to preserve the integrity of our community. Stepping conscientiously through communal connections.

Date/Circle Name: 3/11/25 Community Change Women of Color retreat
Content: We celebrate each other and respect our differences.

Date/Circle Name: 3/11/25 Community Change Women of Color retreat
Content: We cohabitate/live in interconnected circles/communities that embrace and welcome differences among its people, thriving and vulnerable.

Date/Circle Name: 3/11/25 Community Change Women of Color retreat
Content: We live in community and thrive in our collective prosperity.

Date/Circle Name: 3/11/25 Community Change Women of Color retreat
Content: We have safety, abundance, and joy.

This small community has long ago embraced diversity as the key to vibrancy.  You see people of different colors, shades, genders, etc. all welcomed.  People know one another’s names.  Acknowledge, and are truly curious.

We no longer learn about our connection to people through obituaries.  Instead we tell stories and connect with the broader community in such a way that we can feel and intimately know members of the community through our lives.
We embrace differences.  There is a basic human respect for others.
Constellation
All of our needs are held in the commons.

Individual relationships are built around agreements about how we will show up for each other and communicate. Communities are built around agreements. Every community may not have the same set of agreements. Every space may not feel like where we want to do life but by communities, agreements reflect how the people who gravitate to those agreements want to do space. Self-actualization is nourished everywhere because we understand it is critical to knowing what you can agree to.
There is communal and telepathic connectedness.  We trust our guts and intuition again.

A huge sign says “thank you”, greeting everyone. This value is that every day we think about what we are thankful for. The brand is “We Build” as a collective. One = many; we tell our stories and turn the page when they no longer serve us.
No ownership; we reflect off of one another, building a sustainable community where when something is needed, we get it done. We thrive off of each other. There are no levels in power.

Communities and cities would work like ecosystems, each person serving a role for the greater community. All individuals would be loved and cared for within the community. All individuals, and individuals with disabilities would serve strengths-based and valued roles within the community. Everyone would contribute according to their capacity. Resources would fuel the communities in self-sustaining ways.
All communities would practice grounded deep curiosity.

Multi-Generational Cooperative Communities: People hold many and fluid identities where many cultures come together with ease. We appreciate the multitudes that exist within each person. Children run freely through the streets, embodying that it takes a village. Role models of all genders are strong and offer examples of non-binary ways of being, multiple ways of being. No matter who they are or how they identify in their lives – that this is OK. That it is all OK. That we can trust our inner wisdom. We are supportive to the wisdom and inner knowing that calls our children into who they want to be and what they want to do. We support them, knowing that they came into the world with their own wisdom  and inner knowings.
No one is lonely. Community holds all of us
Peace is choosing into what we have in common and dead-ing the rest.  Sometimes you can’t.
Relationships in community and creativity give sweetness to life - simplify and settle into what is already good
Children, elders, the sick, the mentally ill- everyone is cared for in our communities.
Fulfillment comes from community and not commodity, full life with less stuff

The geometry of how we structure our communities supports that. With triangles, people are surrounded and supported with plaza and places where people can come together that are easy to navigate for children and elders. People are surrounded and have their own spaces within the community.
People are reconnected to one another, engaging in mutual support and working together to take care of one another and ensure everyone’s needs are met.

We have global agreement on the quality of the conditions that all human communities should function with (potable water, suitable shelter, education, health & medical support, etc.) and resources are shared globally to ensure that all of our relatives are living at or above those conditions.
We know we are part of an eco-system. Children and elders, multi-generations live together.  All of the housing is clustered.  There are less people, and more balance.
Every time you come in contact with someone you give regard, and tend to what is needed.

There is reciprocity, a felt sense of reciprocity, that are essential to how we move.  We have guiding principles that tend to the needs of the oldest and youngest among us. People only take what they need, that’s part of reciprocity - it goes back and forth. 
Children are raised with their hearts singing.

Surrounded by the natural environment. Access to sovereignty, medicine and health. People are outside, connected to land. We live in multigenerational, multi family dwellings, with vastly different designs. Homes are clay, round, multiple small pods, multiple families sharing land and space. Food and medicine everywhere. There is joy. Lots of people interacting.

Like Star Wars, a representative from one vessel is brought into the new vessel. When someone arrives into the new starship, there is a crowd to greet them. A welcoming, even if there is tension in the air. Borders are like this, spaces of welcome where people are guided and not restricted into a new space. People are welcomed with food and drink, and needs are met. People are received with curiosity.

Only histories and names to remember where we’ve come from. People move freely, welcomed with gifts and kindness. We live in vibrant collectives: birth families, chosen families, friends sharing homes, multigenerational households where care is shared and joy is multiplied. Everyone has a home. Everyone belongs.
Being in this horizon circle, together, reminds us of what life is really about. Finding the courage to imagine creative thriving after a great collapse.

When community members suffer - they do not suffer in silence - the community notices and gathers around them. Isolation and loneliness are met with curiosity and love, not systems and institutions or judgment.
We ask . . . 

When was the last time you danced?
When was the last time you sang?
When was the last time you made art?

We define “we” as deeper and more expansive. 

We are dependent and interdependent as we rely on each other because we can no longer live isolated and independent. There is not an online Amazon, there are only Neighbors.

We create space. We hold space for dialogue and opportunity - for the young and the seasoned.

We know there is value and brightness and wisdom learned and wisdom learning.

Instead of looking at others to judge what's wrong, we extend our thinking to what it is we need to be well. This calls for assessments and action.  

We are curious about each other, instead of afraid.

Healers deep intuition is revered. The ‘’strange ones’’ are held, integrated.

There is deep belief in renewal, the possibility of a new shift of that only juxtaposition can afford us.

Choices of mates is based on entirely different criteria. There is sex. Heart break. People have preferences and there are many ways to be in connection.

Community holds.
Gatherings. Fall is a time of planning.
We ours us mutual care
Sacred attention of how you enter a community
Dedicated time for community. Multiples & abundance. New meaning of family. Not ownership but responsibility communal mindset around care.
People of color know what is like and feels like to be free. A great sense of community. Community, American community, US community. Physical, mental and emotional safety.

We live free. Connected to land. Unconditional love. No one way of doing anything. Love and strength in our scars, connection to ancestral spirit. We ask out loud for the support we need. Local support, including rebuilding ourselves. We learn from elders and community. We are connected to what our blood connects us to.

Concentric circles with a heart (drawing) Rooted in ancestral ways. The human world has a rightful place in the circle. We return to hyperlocalization. There is, we are enough. We know this in our bones.Travel is limited and honors Mother Earth.

We value community.  Little ones move in public, take trains, and ride bikes on their own without any need for “their people” guarding them.   “Their people” is our collective values and practice.  We are all “their people” and at the same time those little ones aren’t bound to our collective expectations as to who they must be.  There is broad room for exploration, experiences, and freedom–all held with reciprocal understanding and care.
People know the names of the people in the community.  They watch out for one another’s needs.

There are ceremonies to honor and appreciate the courage it took for the ancestors to acknowledge that there was no way through but to literally take care of one another…and to think of new ways to resources and participate in that.
We tell stories all the time of how community takes care of community.

Community will move at a slower pace.  Neighbors know neighbors.  There are common shared housing goals.  Buildings and shelters are made from sustainable things.  We help each other–including taking care of young and old.
More than enough for everyone

Who and how you love, what you grow and create is the new currency
Softer, kinder, more smiley
Strangers are family we don’t know yet
The culture of the community celebrates rest and prioritizes this for all people.
People in our communities are living whole, healthy, vibrant and thriving lives.
The community members feel free in articulating any needs. And the rest of the community feel joyful, ready, and capable to help.
This is a meeting that’s occuring in communities, across the world, often in partnership with other communities.
Vibrant and healthy community relationships

The first quarterly meeting of the community council is happening. There’s a lot of excitement, food, and energy. Almost everyone in the community those who have been here for generations, years, some months are gathered.
My world would be interconnected- all the circles connect

We live in communities where people’s needs are met: everyone has the right to housing and food. Even though money exists, basic needs are subsidized by the government with stamps. There are a variety of jobs that people can have to support the functioning of the society, such as crossing guards, driving the trolleys, and working in stores.
We will share resources and live in connected communities – villages of support, love, safety
Ours and us is both small and big, the people, places and beings near to us and also the whole collective. All is held collectively.

Communities are smaller, there are still essential roles. There are farmers, teachers, butchers, leaders, elders. People know each other and check in on each other. People are more attentive and intentional. Time slows down. Options are limited but there’s more than enough for basic needs. More care and deeper connections to see commonalities more than differences. Sustainability is at a smaller scale. We eat seasonal fruits, not from abroad. We are appreciative of what we have and the roles people play to make that happen.
Recognizing and addressing tension points. True community.

In 150 years past the conflict, success is not driven by individual accomplishments but instead by holistic communities. Communities that are based upon selfishness, where inclusion and acceptance of individuality thrive. Instead of a sense of entitlement there is a ground swell of graciousness, respect.  When we look beyond, there is peace and harmony with nature and our world. Truly heaven on earth, health, agelessness sharing of wisdom and joy.  Abundant unconditional love.

At town meetings, we have abandoned clock time. We wake when we wake, not to alarm clocks or factory rhythms. The community values Town Meetings so much that it is a paid holiday for all and you are encouraged to join the community. We create gifts to the town potluck. We are thinking about our contributions to the various topics. We will improvise and find a third way that is  unknown to us until we all participate.

The community comes together to help others when in need. There is a big sense of community. Children are taught from a young age to go together and help when there is a need and autonomy to not participate is honored.

There is a community of small homes with a central kitchen.  Today, some people made muffins, some made coffee.  Others are going out and gathering things that the people need.  There is a community consensus about responsibility to one another.

Communities now have a central space where there is flow – a moving into and away from the center that is replicated in movement in and to other communities, too. Sometimes we need to be in community and sometimes we need to be with ourselves. Community honors this in each of us. We take different roles and different times in community and that is OK.
Resources are pooled and support the whole community.  Resources are used thoughtfully with understanding for the natural world and the wellbeing of all.

Still people do enjoy the duty and desire to contribute and care for the community. We also support each career - more prestigious or not - and ensure material physical needs for everyone in the community are met, as a baseline. We are practicing and getting better at not having hierarchy within roles.
We aren’t the only people who live, eat, and gather this way. There are connected communities of many sizes - some small, some midsize, some big.
We’ve designed our communities focused on how we gather and play, rather than separate ourselves.
We gather for many reasons and across changing seasons. We see value in playing cards, sharing beverages and marijuana - these things and a sense of humor helped get us through.

Dogs may be the most beloved four leggeds in this horizon (they do bring still needed levity) - but we also enjoy and care of many four-leggeds and two-leggeds, of plants, and even some six and eight-legged creatures. When we gather, they gather too.
In Ubuntu Village, happiness flows from harmony among people, earth, and spirit. Everyone belongs, is valued, and needed.  Love and care shape daily life. Food is shared.
For this community, I hold the love and respect ‘beacon’ . I may use a wheelchair,  not speak and see only a little…. But I am home and each person here sits in peace with  me when they need me.

Community members will disagree, but they will never question that they are still a part of the community.  Different beliefs and different morals can offer broader perspectives.  Above all else, though, all are responsible for tending to the wellbeing of the whole community.

There would be the equivalent of vibrant and fun union/company/community picnics that everyone attended.  Everyone would carve out the time to participate, and it would feel like a gathering of interconnected families.  People would have conversational skills and talk about things – including politics.

The community will make rules that are as broadly accepting as possible – but the community takes seriously each individual’s responsibility to the overall wellbeing being of the community.  In other words, people will be supported to live how they want as long as it isn’t hurting others.

Date/Circle Name: 10/29/25 Kailua, HI Kahanaiki Group, Le Jardin Academy
Content: Dream big. Communities of love and kindness. Everyone works together to generate a beautiful place we call home. Trees are tall, shiny, they touch the skies that are full of native birds, singing. The ocean is a different kind of blue now. Families look out for each other. The ocean isn’t rising in heat but settling in its comfort. There is easily accessible medicine and healthcare. The air is clean. The skies are clear.

Date/Circle Name: 10/29/25 Kailua, HI Kahanaiki Group, Le Jardin Academy
Content: Everyone works together no matter what their difference in opinion.

Date/Circle Name: 10/30/25 Kailua, HI Polynesian Club, Le Jardin Academy
Content: Plants have restoration areas, where people in the community are required to help.

Small communities. When we use resources from other communities we don’t have a relationship with, there is relationship building and consent that comes with that use. People feel the impact of the resources they use, in their lives and those of the people they share life with.
We know we are connected.  Practically, we depend on one another.  People grow their own food.
Life is community focused for resilience and thrivingness.  This is taught and guided through embodies action.

We practice interdependence in our spirituality.  It is essential to our connections.  “I am you and you are me” - we have a deep understanding that each of us are relevant and each of us is part of the collective consciousness.  “My spirit is tied up in yours.”  The value of things like borders has fallen based on the value we see in each other.

The Mother can rest and heal fully with the help of community care. All communities will intersect in harmony while respecting differences and boundaries. Communities will lean on and support one another with necessary resources and areas of expertise. You can't do this work alone.

Community agreements are something everyone gets to add to; it can change and fluctuate depending on the people who move in and out of the community. Communities will address harm. There must be community unity on a global level. May we continue to pass these values down to our grandchildren. Leading by example so that our family sees our changes. It fills me with pride. United we can change everything. Yes, we can. A bridge and a red river. Everything with bridges so that everyone can cross. A place where they can enjoy freely for my future generation. The colorful little houses we left behind in our countries exist in the future.
Original of Translation: Tiene que haber unión de comunidad a nivel mundial. Que sigamos transmitiendo esos valores a nuestros nietos. Predicar con el ejemplo para que nuestra familia vea nuestros cambios. Me llena de orgullo. Unidos podemos cambiar todo. Si se Puede. Un puente y un río colorado. Todo con puentes porque pueden pasar todos. Un lugar donde ellos puedan disfrutar libremente para mi futura generacion. Las casitas de colores que dejamos en nuestros paises existen en el futuro.

It’s important that everyone within communities all over the world act as a village since it takes a village  to rase one child. So, imagine the millions, billions of others that could impact majority of the world if we all come together.
